unresolved_candidates.reason: Tobiah and Toubiani resemble one another, but the named communities and the reported fates are not established as identical by these texts.
Chaspho in the list of captured Gileadite towns is not explicitly identified with Caspin, whose fortifications and adjacent lake are described in the proposed target.

A renewed army under Timothy resembles the proposed target, but the death of Timothy in that target and the later Timothy campaign in 2 Maccabees 12 prevent an unqualified personal or episode identity.
The burning of the sacred precinct at Carnaim may be compared with the attack on Carnion and Atargatis, but exact place, sanctuary, and episode identity are not demonstrated by the texts alone.

semantic_observations: Explicit same-chapter labels correctly identify all within-chapter connections.
The four unresolved identity proposals remain unretained with zero credit. Limited comparisons involving Timothy or Carnaim/Carnion do not establish personal, geographical, or episode identity.
Elymais/Persepolis, Babylon/Ecbatana, Beth-zechariah/Modein, military totals, Eupator dates, Philip commissions and destinations, and Nicanor peace negotiations are not forcibly harmonized.
Greek Psalm 78 numbering is retained. The 1 Samuel 17 passage uses actual extant units and invents neither verse 41 nor verse 50.
The conquest comparisons concern specified narrative actions. The land Sabbath and royal sacrifice comparisons do not assert extra legal permissions.
The bronze tablet and Roman friendship comparisons were checked in their wider Roman and Spartan diplomatic context.

Both original peer findings are resolved. The full original review and exact original packet and author receipt are preserved, including the separate read-timing precision addendum. Final acceptance binds the corrected TSV and final author receipt.

source_verse.text: Judas fought against the sons of Esau in Idumea, in Akrabattene, because they were besieging Israel. He struck them a great blow, subdued them, and took their spoils.

target_verses.text: Along with him, the Idumeans, who held strategic fortresses, harassed the Jews. Taking in those driven from Jerusalem, they attempted to maintain the war.
Maccabeus and his men offered an entreaty and asked God to become their ally; then they rushed against the Idumean fortresses.
Attacking them vigorously, they gained control of the places, drove off all who fought on the wall, and slaughtered those they encountered. They killed no fewer than twenty thousand.

row.rationale: The judgment that Israelite collaborators inflicted exceptional harm develops the book's earlier account of lawless Israelites persuading their people to abandon the covenant for foreign customs.

source_verse.text: Judas saw all the evil that Alcimus and those with him had committed among the sons of Israel, beyond that of the nations.

target_verses.text: In those days lawless sons came out of Israel and persuaded many, saying, “Let us go and make a covenant with the nations around us, because since we separated ourselves from them, many evils have overtaken us.”
The proposal was good in their eyes.
Some of the people eagerly went to the king, and he gave them authority to follow the ordinances of the nations.
They built a gymnasium in Jerusalem according to the customs of the nations
and made foreskins for themselves. They abandoned the holy covenant, yoked themselves to the nations, and sold themselves to do evil.
